items.headline: M'luru in the running for 50-acre cricket hub
items.blurb: Mangaluru Urban Development Authority and Karnataka State Cricket Association are evaluating government land parcels of about 25–50 acres, including sites near Kenjar, Gurupura bridge and New Mangaluru Port Authority, for a proposed cricket stadium.

items.headline: Drunk-driving Mini Cooper crash kills 3, including M'luru youth
items.blurb: Three people died in Nedumbassery, Kochi, when a Mini Cooper allegedly driven under the influence by Suhail Sajeer hit a two-wheeler; a Mangaluru youth was among the victims.

items.headline: Koragas stage semi-nude protest seeking title deeds
items.blurb: Koraga community members marched semi-nude to the Deputy Commissioner's office in Padil, Mangaluru, demanding title deeds and house sites promised earlier.

items.headline: AERA to hold tariff consultation for Mangaluru airport
items.blurb: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority scheduled a stakeholders' meeting on October 15, 2026, on aeronautical tariffs for Mangaluru International Airport for the second control period 2024–2031.

items.headline: Students protest against college opposing UG semester exams during Dasara
items.blurb: Students of St Agnes College (Autonomous), backed by ABVP, protested undergraduate semester exams scheduled during Dasara; the college postponed papers set for October 19 and 22.

items.headline: 'Digital arrest' scam strips farmer of ₹1.31 cr
items.blurb: A 52-year-old farmer from Puttur lost ₹1.31 crore to fraudsters posing as Mumbai Police and ATS officers who claimed he was linked to terrorist money laundering.

items.headline: DK child protection unit to probe sexual abuse charge against church priest
items.blurb: The Dakshina Kannada District Child Protection Unit is investigating allegations that a church priest sexually abused a minor girl.

items.headline: Mescom chairman asks KPTCL to supply quality power
items.blurb: Mescom chairman K. Harish Kumar, inspecting the new 400 kV sub-station at Kadandale in Moodbidri taluk, Dakshina Kannada, on Friday, instructed KPTCL to ensure uninterrupted, quality power to the coastal region. KPTCL Superintending Engineer Chaitanya said the project aims to supply major industrial hubs and permanently address monsoon voltage fluctuations and low-voltage issues.

items.headline: Rare two-year-old male black leopard trapped in cage
items.blurb: Forest officials trapped a rare black leopard in Shirlalu village, Belthangady, and planned to release it into protected forest after a health check.

items.headline: Don't take part in Mysuru Dasara Kambala: KRRS
items.blurb: Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha State president Badagalapura Nagendra, addressing press persons in Mangaluru on Monday, urged coastal buffalo owners registered for Mysuru Dasara Kambala on October 18 and 19 to cancel and withdraw. He cited severe drought and dry lakes, destruction of a former park site’s ecosystem including more than 50 trees, and citizens’ grievance that other Dasara events are not organised systematically.

items.headline: K'taka High Court strikes down 56% quota for SC/ST
items.blurb: The Karnataka High Court struck down the 2022 amendment raising Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reservations to 56%, holding it unconstitutional for breaching the Supreme Court's 50% ceiling on quotas.

items.headline: Sudha Yadav new Governor of K'taka
items.blurb: Senior BJP leader Sudha Yadav was appointed Governor of Karnataka, succeeding Thawar Chand Gehlot.

items.headline: Rs 9k cr sanctioned for Konkan Railway: Somanna
items.blurb: Union Minister V Somanna said ₹9,000 crore has been sanctioned for Konkan Railway works on the route serving coastal Karnataka.

items.headline: Difficult to meet TN's Cauvery demand: K'taka
items.blurb: Karnataka told the Supreme Court it cannot meet Tamil Nadu's Cauvery water demand in a rain-deficit year and asked how backlog could be cleared.

items.headline: Post 42.29 lakh hearings, 33,547 voters found 'ineligible'
items.blurb: After 42.29 lakh hearings in Karnataka's voter-roll revision, 33,547 names were deleted as ineligible; the final list is to be published on October 27.

items.headline: Oppn files plea against CEC; thousands join march to SC
items.blurb: I.N.D.I.A leaders and supporters marched in New Delhi to the Supreme Court to file a plea against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list irregularities; police did not interfere as on previous days, and the court is to hear the plea soon.

items.headline: No more protests at Jantar Mantar; 3 new sites named
items.blurb: Delhi Police have barred protests at Jantar Mantar and designated three alternative sites—Rohini/Bawana, CBD Ground East District and Burari Ground North District—for demonstrations.

items.headline: Food, fuel push retail inflation to 23-month high of 5.54%
items.blurb: Retail inflation hit a 23-month high of 5.54% as food prices—including vegetables such as tomatoes and lemons—and fuel-linked transport costs rose sharply.

items.headline: Top LeT man among four killed in Poonch minefield
items.blurb: Four Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists, including commander Muhammad Faizaz, died in a mine blast while trying to cross the LoC in Poonch.

items.headline: Alterations to Form 6 made after ruling on Bihar SIR: SC
items.blurb: The Supreme Court clarified its stance on alterations to Form 6 (voter registration) following a July 27 ruling on the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.

items.headline: Skies over Saudi capital empty after deadly Houthi strikes
items.blurb: Flight operations at Riyadh's international airport were suspended after drone and missile strikes attributed to Houthi rebels.

items.headline: Economics Nobel to Robert Hall, Woodford
items.blurb: American economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford were awarded the economics Nobel for work on stabilization models, the front page reported.

items.headline: Airbase plot 'directed' by Iran Guards: UK PM
items.blurb: UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak said a foiled plot against a British airbase was almost certainly directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

items.headline: Bangladesh, China ink loan deal to modernise port near Indian border
items.blurb: Bangladesh signed a $535.78 million Chinese Exim Bank loan to upgrade Mongla Port, raising Indian concerns over Beijing's footprint near the border.

items.headline: Over 100 foreign trekkers stranded in Nepal floods
items.blurb: Flooding after a glacier collapse in central Nepal killed many people and left more than 100 foreign trekkers stranded.

items.headline: Rahul and Revanth send Karnataka on a leather hunt
items.blurb: Debutant S.V. Rahul (unbeaten 108 off 187 balls, 10 fours) and Revanth Reddy (97 off 143) shared a 202-run sixth-wicket stand as Andhra closed day two on 331 for six, a 57-run lead over Karnataka’s 274, in the Ranji Trophy opener at Mulapadu. Andhra had been 116 for five after Shaik Rasheed’s 54; Shikhar Shetty took three wickets and Madhav Bajaj two for an inexperienced Karnataka attack that bowled only seven maidens in 90 overs.

items.headline: Kushagra replaces Pant in India A squad
items.blurb: Wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra replaces rested Rishabh Pant in the India A squad.

items.headline: Tough opener for Sindhu
items.blurb: P V Sindhu faces world No 1 An Se-young in the Denmark Open opener; Lakshya Sen also returns in men's singles.

items.headline: Plan to shackle Hope executed to perfection: Arshdeep
items.blurb: Arshdeep Singh took three wickets in Indore as India beat West Indies in the third T20I to lead the series 2–1, saying the plan against Shai Hope worked.

items.headline: RANJI TROPHY SCORES — ROUND ONE, DAY TWO
items.blurb: Round-one day-two scores included Uttar Pradesh 540 (Madhav Kaushik 150, Rinku Singh 112) vs Bihar 44/2 at Rajgir; Vidarbha 428 (Akshay Wadkar 199, Yash Rathod 134) vs Pondicherry 107/1 at Nagpur; Hyderabad 294 (Sandip Sarkar 8/96) vs Tripura 134 and 106/7; Karnataka 274 vs Andhra 331/6 at Vijayawada; Saurashtra 392 (Prerak Mankad 129, Ravindra Jadeja 102) vs Chhattisgarh 122/3; Jharkhand 587 vs Kerala at Jamshedpur; Bengal 304/3 (Sudip Kumar Gharami 122*, Abishek Porel 114*) vs Delhi 240; and Mumbai 429 vs Chandigarh 78 and 0/1, with Tushar Deshpande taking 5/17 including a hat-trick.
